:football: *Week 1 Recap: Fourteen Teams Enter, Thirteen Immediately Regret It*
_"Nobody's roster is safe. Nobody's ego either."_

:heart-8bit: *League Pulse*
Delivery Red Zone opened its season with a game that made everyone else's blowout look worse by comparison. <@U032LD8RMK8|Marissa Tomko>'s Scott's Tots put up 119.3 and still lost, because <@U09KVP9JHQS|Jesse Chou>'s Goal Line Stand Jesse found 132.1 from somewhere and closed the gap by 12.8. Everywhere else, the customer experience was rougher: five of seven games were decided by 28 points or more. Parity is not this league's problem in Week 1.

:confused-math-lady: *Stat of the Week*
The league average was 117.3. <@U03R72JAKFH|Morgan Nelson>'s Morgan's Team! won its opener with exactly 116.7 — below average, and still a W. Somewhere, six other teams scored more points and have nothing to show for it. Efficiency isn't optional here, apparently, it's optional but conditional on your opponent being worse.


:footballl: *Matchups*

*<@U09KVP9JHQS|Jesse Chou>'s Goal Line Stand Jesse (132.1) def. <@U032LD8RMK8|Marissa Tomko>'s Scott's Tots (119.3)*
_"Closest One All Week"_
Both sides scored well above the league floor, and it still came down to single digits at the buzzer. Marissa's 119.3 would have won four of the other six games outright. This week, it bought a loss and a very reasonable complaint.

*<@U03R72JAKFH|Morgan Nelson>'s Morgan's Team! (116.7) def. <@U08SKVCGDQW|Greg Stewart>'s The Blackberries (97.4)*
_"A Win Is a Win, Allegedly"_
Morgan cleared 116.7 without doing much of anything memorable, which is its own kind of skill. The Blackberries' 97.4 wasn't a disaster, just quietly below the room. Onboarding complete, retention pending.

*<@U0405KM3X7C|Adam Eichorn>'s Hut Hut Eich (121.1) def. <@U07JPH677ED|Joseph Barry>'s Blitz Squad Joseph (92.4)*
_"Comfortable, Not Cute"_
Adam cruised to 121.1 without needing a hero performance — the fantasy equivalent of a routine renewal. Joseph's 92.4 wasn't embarrassing, it just showed up to a fight that had already been decided by kickoff.

*<@U0761N3RYSW|Sachin Phadkar>'s Penalty Flag Sachin (135.8) def. <@U08QHPYDZ46|Adam Strutynski>'s Dasher Mafia (101.0)*
_"Second-Highest Score, Zero Suspense"_
135.8 is a number that should have been the league's marquee performance. Instead it's buried in the middle of the recap because Dasher Mafia's 101.0 never made it interesting. A 34.7-point gap in Week 1 is an early flag on the whole roster.

*<@U03L8KFL1RS|Elisa Keny>'s Monster of the Midway (157.6) def. <@U0AV2EB5GUD|Luis Islas>'s Game of Throws (119.0)*
_"The Number Everyone Else Should Fear"_
157.6 is the highest score in the league by 15 full points, and it came in Week 1, when nobody's supposed to have their playbook figured out yet. Luis's 119.0 was a perfectly fine score that got run over anyway. Bad beat, worse timing.

*<@UPQ8CPJDR|Peter Van Oot>'s High Quality TD Rate (141.5) def. <@U08SD0PJ3EU|Danielle DiRaddo>'s big d's fantasy (101.6)*
_"Exactly What the Team Name Promised"_
Pete backed up the name with the second-best score in the league. danielle's 101.6 wasn't the problem — the 39.8-point gap on the other side of the ledger was. Some weeks the matchup algorithm just isn't your account manager.

*<@U03FE7P8EEP|Tyler Hanlon>'s Purdy Boys (127.4) def. <@U02C39SFXPD|Tim Tang>'s Stiff Arm tim (79.7)*
_"The Blowout With a Bow On It"_
127.4 didn't even need to be great, because Stiff Arm tim's 79.7 was the lowest score anyone posted all week. A 47.7-point margin in the opener is a rough first entry in anyone's win-loss column, let alone their confidence.

:football: *Week 2 Recap: The Bench Had a Better Week Than You*
_"Your lineup is a decision. Your bench is a confession."_

:heart-8bit: *League Pulse*
Open on the closest thing this league had to drama: <@U07JPH677ED|Joseph Barry>'s Blitz Squad Joseph took down <@U02C39SFXPD|Tim Tang>'s Stiff Arm tim, 136.2 to 116.8, a 19.4-point gap that was somehow the nail-biter of the week. The next-closest game wasn't far behind at 19.7, and from there margins climbed straight up to 65.5, which tells you the league's current state: nobody's playing close games, they're just choosing who gets run over. The last gasp of September, and half this league is already gasping.

:confused-math-lady: *Stat of the Week*
<@UPQ8CPJDR|Peter Van Oot>'s High Quality TD Rate moved to 2-0 on 104.5 points, 6.1 below the league average, while Patrick Mahomes produced 29.0 points from the bench. A premium-tier subscription performing like the free trial, and the account still renewed.


:footballl: *Matchups*

*<@U07JPH677ED|Joseph Barry>'s Blitz Squad Joseph (136.2) def. <@U02C39SFXPD|Tim Tang>'s Stiff Arm tim (116.8)*
_"The Closest Thing to Drama"_
This was Week 2's tightest finish, and "tight" here means 19.4 points. Joseph posted his season high; tim's 116.8 was his best output yet too, and it still went in the loss column. Some weeks the schedule is just bad account management.

*<@U03L8KFL1RS|Elisa Keny>'s Monster of the Midway (111.8) def. <@U03R72JAKFH|Morgan Nelson>'s Morgan's Team! (92.1)*
_"Quietly Business as Usual"_
Elisa stayed unbeaten without doing anything Week 1-level impressive, and 111.8 was plenty against Morgan's 92.1. Morgan's Team dropped its first game after opening 1-0 on a below-average total. Churn happens.

*<@U08SKVCGDQW|Greg Stewart>'s The Blackberries (151.3) def. <@U0405KM3X7C|Adam Eichorn>'s Hut Hut Eich (127.3)*
_"Both Sides Actually Showed Up"_
Two teams cleared 125 and only one got a win for it. Adam's 127.3 was the highest score anyone posted in a loss this week. Gregory's 151.3 is the league's second-highest score, and it just bought him a seven-spot jump nobody saw coming.

*<@UPQ8CPJDR|Peter Van Oot>'s High Quality TD Rate (104.5) def. <@U08QHPYDZ46|Adam Strutynski>'s Dasher Mafia (75.4)*
_"A Win Filed Under Miscellaneous"_
Pete's already covered above — a below-average win with a franchise quarterback rotting on the bench. Adam's 75.4 was the second-lowest score of the week; Dasher Mafia's roster needs a retention plan before Week 3.

*<@U0761N3RYSW|Sachin Phadkar>'s Penalty Flag Sachin (133.9) def. <@U0AV2EB5GUD|Luis Islas>'s Game of Throws (92.1)*
_"Sachin's Quietly Building a Case"_
133.9 points, fourth-best in the league this week, and somehow still not the story anyone's telling. Luis's 92.1 wasn't even his worst outing this season, which says more about Game of Throws' floor than the box score can fix.

*<@U08SD0PJ3EU|Danielle DiRaddo>'s big d's fantasy (103.6) def. <@U09KVP9JHQS|Jesse Chou>'s Goal Line Stand Jesse (52.8)*
_"The Low Point, Literally"_
Jesse's 52.8 is the lowest score anyone has posted all season, more than 20 points under the previous floor. Danielle didn't need to be good to win this one. A 50.8-point margin isn't a rivalry. It's a mismatch.

*<@U03FE7P8EEP|Tyler Hanlon>'s Purdy Boys (157.8) def. <@U032LD8RMK8|Marissa Tomko>'s Scott's Tots (92.3)*
_"The Gap Between First and Last"_
Tyler's 157.8 is this week's high mark, and the 65.5-point margin over Marissa is the widest of the young season. Marissa is 0-2 with a point differential heading toward a performance review. Tyler read the onboarding deck twice.

:football: *Week 3 Recap: Perfect Records Meet Their Bench*
_"Three weeks in, and the league's tanking teams have already found their floor. Turns out it's lower than expected."_

:heart-8bit: *League Pulse*
<@U09KVP9JHQS|Jesse Chou>'s Goal Line Stand Jesse survived <@U08QHPYDZ46|Adam Strutynski>'s Dasher Mafia by 3.2 points in the tightest game of the week — the nicest thing that's happened to Dasher Mafia all season. Elsewhere, three teams sit at 3-0, three sit at 0-3, and the last gasp of September mostly meant everyone's roster looked as tired as their group chat. The gap between the league's contenders and its cellar is starting to look less like parity and more like a customer segmentation exercise nobody asked for.

:confused-math-lady: *Stat of the Week*
Vegas had <@U0761N3RYSW|Sachin Phadkar>'s Penalty Flag Sachin favored over <@U03L8KFL1RS|Elisa Keny>'s Monster of the Midway by 7.56 projected points. Monster of the Midway won by 10.52 anyway — an 18.08-point round trip from what the projections promised, powered by Garrett Wilson going off for 26.7 while Sachin left 21.0 points of Kalif Raymond sitting on his own bench.

:footballl: *Matchups*

*<@U09KVP9JHQS|Jesse Chou>'s Goal Line Stand Jesse (105.3) def. <@U08QHPYDZ46|Adam Strutynski>'s Dasher Mafia (102.1)*
_So Close, Yet So 0-3_
Bijan Robinson posted 35.3 by himself, which is the only reason this team is 2-1 instead of buried with everyone else. Dasher Mafia got a shockingly good Tyler Shough game (24.8) and still lost by 3.2, a bad beat dressed up as a coin flip. Three straight losses now, each one closer than the last, like the season is slow-walking them to the edge.

*<@U03FE7P8EEP|Tyler Hanlon>'s Purdy Boys (128.0) def. <@U08SD0PJ3EU|Danielle DiRaddo>'s big d's fantasy (122.6)*
_Undefeated, Unbothered_
Chris Olave and benched Terry McLaurin somehow tied at 19.7 points apiece, which tells you Purdy Boys' depth chart is basically a coin with two winning sides. Brock Purdy threw for 31.3 on the other side, and it still wasn't enough. Retention strategy: retaining first place.

*<@U0405KM3X7C|Adam Eichorn>'s Hut Hut Eich (110.3) def. <@U03R72JAKFH|Morgan Nelson>'s Morgan's Team! (104.2)*
_The Kicker Outscored Three Starters_
Spencer Shrader put up 17 points for Morgan's Team, either a great week for the kicker or a rough one for everybody drafted ahead of him. George Kittle's 26.2 wasn't enough cover. Hut Hut Eich won on the strength of a tight end (Harold Fannin Jr., 24.1) and a bench so deep that Malik Willis (11.0) and Greg Dulcich (10.5) both cleared double digits without playing a snap.

*<@U03L8KFL1RS|Elisa Keny>'s Monster of the Midway (103.2) def. <@U0761N3RYSW|Sachin Phadkar>'s Penalty Flag Sachin (92.7)*
_The Upset Nobody Projected_
The betting favorite lost anyway, undone by a lineup that started Devaughn Vele (6.9) and the Bengals defense (3.0) over a 21-point Kalif Raymond game sitting one click away on the bench. Conversion funnel working perfectly — converting a favorite into a loser.

*<@U032LD8RMK8|Marissa Tomko>'s Scott's Tots (143.9) def. <@U07JPH677ED|Joseph Barry>'s Blitz Squad Joseph (127.2)*
_Jahmyr Gibbs Has Notes_
Gibbs went for 41.4 points alone, the single-player line of the week, pushing Scott's Tots to the league's highest score by a wide margin. Blitz Squad Joseph, meanwhile, started Bo Nix (25.1) over a benched Sam Darnold (29.7), a self-inflicted Bench Hero nomination if there ever was one. A/B tested this lineup. Both variants still lost.

*<@U08SKVCGDQW|Greg Stewart>'s The Blackberries (130.2) def. <@U02C39SFXPD|Tim Tang>'s Stiff Arm tim (111.1)*
_Two Tight Ends, One Regret_
Jaxon Smith-Njigba's 35.4 did the heavy lifting, and Brock Bowers put up 27.6 points on the bench behind a starting tight end who managed 12.2 — customer acquisition cost on a position nobody needed to double up on. Ja'Marr Chase's 24.8 kept Stiff Arm tim respectable in a loss that dropped them to 0-3.

*<@UPQ8CPJDR|Peter Van Oot>'s High Quality TD Rate (124.2) def. <@U0AV2EB5GUD|Luis Islas>'s Game of Throws (85.1)*
_The Blowout of the Week_
39.2 points separated these two, the widest margin in the league this week, and High Quality TD Rate didn't even need its full bench: Wan'Dale Robinson (18.7) and Keenan Allen (18.3) never left the sideline. Game of Throws posted the league's lowest score and got actively negative production from a Packers defense that finished at -2.0. Churn rate: 100% of this roster's playoff hopes.

recap:
:football: *Week 4 Recap: The Upset, the Blowout, and the Bench*
_"This week, the best player on four different rosters never left the sideline."_

:heart-8bit: *League Pulse*
Open on the night's closest math problem: <@U02C39SFXPD>'s Stiff Arm tim needed only 129.2 to beat <@U0405KM3X7C>'s Hut Hut Eich's 126.2, winning by just 3.0 after Yahoo had Hut Hut Eich favored by 7.6. It's peak October, when the standings start meaning something, and apparently nobody told the Week 4 projections. Elsewhere, <@UPQ8CPJDR>'s High Quality TD Rate moved to 4-0 by beating <@U03L8KFL1RS>'s Monster of the Midway by 74.6, the kind of score usually reserved for a bye week.

:confused-math-lady: *Stat of the Week*
<@U08SD0PJ3EU>'s big d's fantasy lost to <@U07JPH677ED>'s Blitz Squad Joseph by 13.64 points with Kyle Monangai's 28.0 sitting on the bench. Swap him in for Quentin Johnston's 5.0 at flex, and she wins by 9.36 instead of losing by 13.64 — a 23-point gap that flipped the entire outcome.

:footballl: *Matchups*

*<@U02C39SFXPD>'s Stiff Arm tim (129.2) def. <@U0405KM3X7C>'s Hut Hut Eich (126.2)*
_Vegas Had Notes_
Projected to lose by 7.6, tim won anyway behind Zay Flowers' 25.8 and a kicker who outscored Ja'Marr Chase's whole night. <@U0405KM3X7C>'s CeeDee Lamb put up 41.3, the week's second-best individual game, and it still wasn't enough — Josh Downs' flex spot managed 4.6 while Khalil Shakir's 13.2 watched from the bench.

*<@U08QHPYDZ46>'s Dasher Mafia (97.8) def. <@U03FE7P8EEP>'s Purdy Boys (89.7)*
_The Streak Ends, Quietly_
Three weeks of invincibility for <@U03FE7P8EEP>'s Purdy Boys ended against the league's actual last-place team, helped along by a flex spot that started Terry McLaurin for zero while Deebo Samuel put up 18.0 from the bench. Dasher Mafia's 97.8 was 17 points under the league average and still good enough — the week's clearest luckiest win. Saquon Barkley scored 2.0 for the winners, who needed Ashton Jeanty's 18.6 to make it stand. Dasher Mafia's first real retention win of the season.

*<@U07JPH677ED>'s Blitz Squad Joseph (145.4) def. <@U08SD0PJ3EU>'s big d's fantasy (131.7)*
_One Player, 45 Points, Zero Explanation Needed_
Tetairoa McMillan went off for 45.2, the single-biggest individual game anyone posted this week, and carried Joseph to the league's top score. He started Bo Nix over a benched Sam Darnold for the second week running, a decision that cost him in Week 3 and nearly cost him again — danielle's big d's fantasy would've won this one by 9.36 with one smarter flex call.

*<@U032LD8RMK8>'s Scott's Tots (129.2) def. <@U08SKVCGDQW>'s The Blackberries (102.2)*
_Marissa Rosters Four Kickers. Four._
Somehow Scott's Tots carries four kickers and started the one who scored least (6.0) while Cam Little (14.0) and Cairo Santos (11.0) sat idle — four kickers on the books, zero inventory discipline. Javonte Williams' 31.3 did the actual winning regardless. The Blackberries left Romeo Doubs (23.8) and Kirk Cousins (23.6) combined on the bench, 47.4 points that never got a chance to matter.

*<@U0761N3RYSW>'s Penalty Flag Sachin (120.6) def. <@U03R72JAKFH>'s Morgan's Team! (93.2)*
_The Robinson Left Behind_
Sachin won comfortably while Brian Robinson's 25.7 sat on the bench behind a Woody Marks line that managed 8.2, harmless this week but a problem waiting to happen. Morgan's two starting wide receivers combined for 3.3 points, including a flat zero from Ladd McConkey, and Kyler Murray never found enough help to close the gap.

*<@U0AV2EB5GUD>'s Game of Throws (134.8) def. <@U09KVP9JHQS>'s Goal Line Stand Jesse (107.0)*
_The Trap Game Snapped Shut_
Last week's preview called this a trap for "a team that only shows up when Bijan Robinson does." Bijan went for 27.7 again, and Jesse's Goal Line Stand lost by 27.78 anyway because Breece Hall contributed exactly nothing. Game of Throws won despite its own defense actively subtracting three points, proof that ugly wins still count the same as pretty ones.

*<@UPQ8CPJDR>'s High Quality TD Rate (137.6) def. <@U03L8KFL1RS>'s Monster of the Midway (63.0)*
_The Floor Finally Found Elisa_
Monster of the Midway opened the season 3-0 and crashed into Week 4 with the league's lowest score, while Travis Kelce (3.5) and a flex spot that managed zero did approximately nothing. High Quality TD Rate moved to 4-0 behind Kyren Williams' 36.7 and Puka Nacua's 27.7, winning by 74.6 points — the week's biggest margin, with Ollie Gordon's 18.0 stranded on Elisa's bench the entire time.

_"Your lineup card, read anonymously, would still identify you."_

:heart-8bit: *League Pulse*
Fourteen teams, and only 1.8 points separated <@U09KVP9JHQS|Jesse>'s Goal Line Stand Jesse from <@U03L8KFL1RS|Elisa>'s Monster of the Midway — the kind of margin that makes every lineup decision retroactively unbearable. Jesse won it with two starters, Breece Hall and DJ Moore, combining for exactly zero points, which tells you how deep this league's been pushed five weeks in. Elsewhere, <@UPQ8CPJDR|Pete>'s High Quality TD Rate moved to 5-0, a retention rate on winning the rest of the league can't touch, while seven teams, including both sides of that nail-biter, are packed at 3-2. It's officially peak October, when the standings start meaning something.

:confused-math-lady: *Stat of the Week*
<@U03L8KFL1RS|Elisa>'s Monster of the Midway lost by 1.8 points while starting Travis Kelce at tight end for 0.0, with Pat Freiermuth sitting on her bench at 21.5. That's a 21.5-point gap, roughly twelve times the actual margin of defeat, in a slot she filled herself.

_<@U09KVP9JHQS|Jesse>'s Goal Line Stand Jesse (108.8) def. <@U03L8KFL1RS|Elisa>'s Monster of the Midway (107.0)_
_Decided By Less Than a Field Goal_
Jesse survived with Breece Hall and DJ Moore combining for zero and still had enough from Malik Nabers' 29.1 to escape. Elisa's issue wasn't bad luck — it was a benched Pat Freiermuth (21.5) losing his roster spot to a Travis Kelce who scored nothing, a swap that would've flipped this one on its own.

_<@U0AV2EB5GUD|Luis>'s Game of Throws (112.2) def. <@U03FE7P8EEP|Tyler>'s Purdy Boys (103.9)_
_Projections, Overruled_
Yahoo had Tyler favored by 7.3 points. Luis won by 8.3 anyway, riding a 32.4-point Isaiah Likely game while benching Drake Maye's 39.5, this week's Bench Hero nomination, from the winning side. Tyler's second straight loss after opening 3-0 came with Blake Corum (16.2) outscoring both starting running backs from the bench.

_<@U032LD8RMK8|Marissa>'s Scott's Tots (120.9) def. <@U0405KM3X7C|Adam>'s Hut Hut Eich (113.1)_
_Still Four Kickers Deep_
Marissa's bench still carries three unused kickers behind Cam Little's actual 9 points, inventory nobody's forced her to liquidate yet. Jahmyr Gibbs' 37.7 did the real work. Adam answered with Mike Evans (26.3), but Khalil Shakir (11.0) and Greg Dulcich (9.7) sat the whole game behind a CeeDee Lamb (2.9) and Harold Fannin (1.4) who started instead — 20.7 points parked on the bench.

_<@U07JPH677ED|Joseph>'s Blitz Squad Joseph (124.0) def. <@U08QHPYDZ46|adam>'s Dasher Mafia (99.7)_

Joseph's flex gamble on Parker Washington paid out 30.4, more than McCaffrey's 17.3, while the receiver who torched the league for 45.2 in Week 4, Tetairoa McMillan, scored zero from the bench this time. adam got a real 28.94 from Jared Goff and 23 points from a kicker quietly outplaying most of the roster, and Saquon Barkley's zero from the bench did nothing to close the gap.

_<@UPQ8CPJDR|Pete>'s High Quality TD Rate (157.0) def. <@U0761N3RYSW|Sachin>'s Penalty Flag Sachin (122.7)_
_The Rich Get Richer, and Also Bored_
Pete's unbeaten run hit 5-0 behind the week's highest score, and he still had Jayden Daniels (32.3) parked behind Aaron Rodgers on the bench, a luxury tax he can clearly afford. Sachin's Josh Allen threw for 31.5 and George Pickens added 28.0, a score that would've beaten three of this week's other six winners outright, just not the one standing across from it.

_<@U08SKVCGDQW|Gregory>'s The Blackberries (137.7) def. <@U08SD0PJ3EU|danielle>'s big d's fantasy (97.5)_

danielle's 97.5 was the week's lowest score, nearly 20 points under the league average, despite correctly starting Brock Purdy over a 13-point Jalen Hurts on her own bench. :football: *Week 6 Recap: Four Zeroes and a Miracle*
_"Nothing in this league's projections survived first contact this week."_

:heart-8bit: *League Pulse*
Open on the only game that mattered by inches: <@U09KVP9JHQS>'s Goal Line Stand Jesse needed just 7.54 points to beat <@U0761N3RYSW>'s Penalty Flag Sachin, and somehow did it with four starting slots scoring zero: Breece Hall, DJ Moore, Quinshon Judkins, and the Lions defense. Yahoo had Sachin favored by 46.84 points. Yahoo was wrong by a lot. Elsewhere, <@UPQ8CPJDR>'s High Quality TD Rate took its first loss of the season after opening 5-0 — proof that even a perfect retention record eventually churns.

:confused-math-lady: *Stat of the Week*
Christian McCaffrey posted the week's single best individual performance, 30.7 points, and it happened in a 45.12-point loss, the second-widest margin of the week. A great running back game. A completely irrelevant one.


:footballl: *Matchups*

*<@U09KVP9JHQS>'s Goal Line Stand Jesse (94.14) def. <@U0761N3RYSW>'s Penalty Flag Sachin (86.6)*
_How Does a 46-Point Underdog Even Do That?_
Malik Nabers (28.5), Trevor Lawrence (28.34), and Kyle Pitts (23.0) combined for 79.84 points, nearly Jesse's entire total, while Matthew Golden's 22.4 and Jordan Love's 21.24 sat on the bench doing nothing for anyone. Sachin's own tight end, Darren Waller, matched Jesse's dead-weight starters with a zero of his own. Being a 46.84-point favorite and losing by 7.54 is its own category of bad beat.

*<@U08SD0PJ3EU>'s big d's fantasy (97.56) def. <@U0405KM3X7C>'s Hut Hut Eich (88.4)*
_Won Without a Quarterback_
Adam's only options at quarterback were Lamar Jackson, on IR, and Malik Willis, who scored 0.0 off the bench, so Hut Hut Eich effectively played the week at zero under center and still put up 88.4 behind D'Andre Swift's 23.0. danielle needed every bit of Brock Purdy's 17.36 and James Cook's 24.3 for the 9.16-point win, helped along by Khalil Shakir's 13.4 sitting untouched on Adam's bench.

*<@U032LD8RMK8>'s Scott’s Tots (96.76) def. <@U02C39SFXPD>'s Stiff Arm tim (79.24)*
_Two Zeros and Still Comfortable_
Marissa started a running back and a tight end (Jeremiyah Love and Tyler Warren) who combined for exactly zero and still won, her 96.76 finishing below the week's 97.84 league average anyway. Germie Bernard (25.7) and DK Metcalf (20.3) covered for both dead roster spots twice over. tim didn't make a single glaring mistake; a mostly clean lineup still wasn't enough against two receivers outplaying his entire team.

*<@U03R72JAKFH>'s Morgan's Team! (117.16) def. <@UPQ8CPJDR>'s High Quality TD Rate (81.48)*
_The Unbeaten Find Their Mortality_
Pete's first loss of the season arrived with Jayden Daniels (21.0) and Keenan Allen (16.2) combining for more points on his own bench than his actual margin of defeat. Tre Tucker's 26.7 and George Kittle's 17.9 did the damage for a Morgan's Team that improved to just 2-4 and still ended the league's only perfect record in the same afternoon.

*<@U08QHPYDZ46>'s Dasher Mafia (127.86) def. <@U08SKVCGDQW>'s The Blackberries (91.12)*
_Tyler Shough Remembered He's a Starting Quarterback_
Tyler Shough threw and ran his way to 26.96, the best number on a Dasher Mafia roster with four separate contributors in double digits. Gregory's Blackberries got a real game from Jaxon Smith-Njigba (25.4), undercut by a benched Kirk Cousins (19.52) outscoring starter Dak Prescott (13.02) by 6.5 and a benched Michael Mayer (16.5) outscoring starting tight end Brock Bowers (11.0) by 5.5. Two avoidable gaps turned a competitive roster into a 36.74-point churn event.

*<@U0AV2EB5GUD>'s Game of Throws (131.7) def. <@U07JPH677ED>'s Blitz Squad Joseph (86.58)*
_The Bo Nix Decision, Round Three_
Joseph started Bo Nix (4.48) over a benched Sam Darnold (13.02) for at least the third time this season, the same call that already cost him in Weeks 3 and 4. Christian McCaffrey's 30.7 was the best individual game in the league this week, and it still wasn't close: Kenneth Walker (27.9), Isaiah Likely (23.9), and Drake Maye (23.8) spread Luis's damage across the whole lineup instead of leaning on one man.

_The Week's Biggest Blowout, Filed Under Routine_
Tyler won by 57.4, the week's widest margin, while Stefon Diggs (16.4) sat on his bench the entire game, a luxury that never needed cashing in. Elisa's receiving corps gave her 8.4 points from Garrett Wilson, her nominal WR1, and a flat zero from Ollie Gordon at running back. C.J. Stroud's 23.98 was the only part of the box score worth printing.
